cosmetologist.intro: Learn skincare, nail care, and beauty treatments. Build a client base through consistent quality and a clean, professional studio.

skillDomains.name: Skin Care
skillDomains.description: Understand the skin before treating it.

skills.name: Skin Assessment
skills.description: Read the skin before you touch it.

modules.title: The four skin types
modules.content:
Normal

Balanced oil and moisture. Small pores. Rarely breaks out.

Dry

Tight feeling, flaky, sometimes rough.

Oily

Shiny, especially in the T-zone. Enlarged pores. Prone to blackheads and acne.

Combination

Oily in the T-zone, normal or dry elsewhere. Most common skin type.

Plus sensitivities

Some skin reacts to certain ingredients or has conditions like rosacea, eczema, or psoriasis.

modules.title: Running a skin consultation
modules.content:
Ask before treating

  • What products do you currently use?
  • Any allergies or sensitivities?
  • Any medications?
  • Recent waxing, peels, or treatments?
  • Pregnant or breastfeeding?

Observe

  • Skin type and condition
  • Skin tone and undertone
  • Areas of concern
  • Any visible skin conditions

The honest rule

If you see something you don't recognise, refer to a dermatologist.

steps.q: A client's T-zone is shiny but cheeks are flaky. What skin type?
steps.f: Oily T-zone with dry cheeks is combination skin.

steps.q: A pregnant client wants a chemical peel. What do you do?
o: Refuse — many peel ingredients are unsafe in pregnancy
Ask them to sign a waiver
steps.f: Peel ingredients like salicylic and retinoic acid are unsafe in pregnancy.

steps.q: You see a client with red, inflamed patches and flaking. What do you do?
steps.f: Inflammatory skin conditions need medical assessment.

skills.name: Facials
skills.description: The core treatment of any skin studio.

modules.title: The facial sequence
modules.content:
Steps

  1. Consultation — assess skin and goals
  2. Cleanse — remove makeup and surface oils
  3. Exfoliate — gentle removal of dead skin
  4. Steam and extract — soften pores, clear blackheads
  5. Massage — relaxes and increases circulation
  6. Mask — tailored to skin type
  7. Moisturise and SPF — always finish with sun protection

Duration

A basic facial takes 45-60 minutes.

Frequency

Every 4-6 weeks matches the skin's renewal cycle.

steps.q: A client with dry skin wants a purifying mask. What do you do?
o: Explain that purifying masks worsen dry skin; offer a hydrating mask instead
steps.f: Match the treatment to the skin type.

steps.q: During extraction, the client winces in pain. What do you do?
o: Stop, reduce pressure, and only extract what comes easily
steps.f: Extraction should be uncomfortable but not painful.

steps.q: You finish a facial. What's the final step?
steps.f: Always finish with moisturiser AND SPF.

modules.title: Write a facial protocol
modules.prompt: Write out your standard facial protocol from start to finish. Include timings, products, and aftercare instructions.
steps: List every step with the time it takes
Name the products you use and why
Test the protocol on a friend or client

skillDomains.name: Nail Care
skillDomains.description: Manicures and pedicures — the most requested treatments.

skills.name: Manicure
skills.description: Care for the hands and nails.

modules.title: The manicure sequence
modules.content:
Basic manicure

  1. Remove old polish
  2. File nails to shape
  3. Soak hands in warm water
  4. Push back cuticles gently
  5. Trim cuticles (only if needed)
  6. Massage hands with lotion
  7. Apply base coat, colour, top coat

Variations

  • Gel polish — longer lasting, cured under UV
  • Acrylic extensions — sculpted tips
  • Nail art — designs, patterns

Hygiene

All tools sanitised between clients. Files and buffers are single-use or disinfected.

steps.q: You see a client with yellow, thickened, crumbling toenails. What do you do?
o: Refer to a doctor — likely fungal infection
steps.f: Fungal nail infections need medical treatment.

steps.q: A client's cuticle bleeds while you're pushing it back. What do you do?
o: Stop, apply antiseptic, cover the cut, replace single-use tools
steps.f: Any break in skin stops the service.

steps.q: How should you disinfect metal nail tools between clients?

modules.title: The pedicure sequence
modules.content:
Basic pedicure

  1. Remove old polish
  2. Soak feet in warm water with salts
  3. Trim and file nails straight across
  4. Push back cuticles
  5. Remove calluses with pumice or file
  6. Massage feet and lower legs
  7. Apply polish or leave natural

Health considerations

  • Diabetics need extra care
  • Ingrown nails should be handled by a podiatrist if severe
  • Any wound or infection — refer to a doctor

steps.q: A diabetic client wants a pedicure. What extra care do you take?
o: Extra caution — check feet for wounds, don't cut cuticles, use gentle tools
steps.f: Diabetics have reduced sensation and slower healing.

steps.q: A client has an ingrown toenail that looks infected. What do you do?
o: Refer to a doctor or podiatrist
steps.f: Infected ingrown nails need medical treatment.

steps.q: How do you trim toenails correctly?
o: Straight across with slight corner rounding

skillDomains.name: Hygiene & Client Care
skillDomains.description: The standards that protect clients and your business.

modules.title: Why sanitation matters
modules.content:
Beauty treatments involve close contact and broken skin. Without proper sanitation you can transfer:

  • Fungal infections (nail fungus, athlete's foot)
  • Bacterial infections (staph, impetigo)
  • Blood-borne viruses (hepatitis B and C)

What must be sanitised between clients

  • All metal tools — hospital-grade solution
  • Files and buffers — single-use or disinfect
  • Brushes — wash and disinfect
  • Towels — wash hot between clients
  • Surfaces — wipe with disinfectant

steps.q: You drop a metal tool on the floor. Can you use it on the next client?
A nail file has been used on one client. Can you use it on the next?
o: No — files are single-use or must be disinfected
steps.f: Files harbour bacteria. Single-use is safest.

steps.q: You notice a client's skin has a red, infected-looking patch. What do you do?
o: Refer to a doctor — do not treat infected skin
steps.f: Infected skin can spread. Refer out.

modules.title: What brings clients back
modules.content:
The three drivers

  1. Result — they like how they look and feel
  2. Experience — the appointment was pleasant, on time, and comfortable
  3. Relationship — they trust you

How to build all three

  • Consistent quality
  • Remember preferences
  • Follow-up: message 3 days after a facial
  • Recommend a routine they can maintain at home
  • Be on time
  • Never gossip about other clients
